surfaces.part: seamless earth ground field with clods, grit and rust flakes

The column scans show noisy dirt tones with no structural banding. Clods, grit and rust flakes are scattered across the field. It reads as organic ground, not a sticker. Measured facts: 5 visible tones per tile, above the grass reference (3) and below paving (7). Near-flat coverage is 1%, so there are no big flat fills. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the darker clod edges are tinted brown, not black. There are only 12 distinct colours in total, against 80 in the grass reference, and the shading is a limited ramp of about 5 brown steps. Texture is somewhat repetitive and blotchy, with soft, noisy clumps and few crisp per-clod highlights or shaded grit stones. The grit clusters are sparse, so the surface feels a little thinner than the Beodeul grass, which has distinct tufts and clumps. The brief also mentions gravel and rust-flake tiles. These appear only as scattered specks, not as distinct tiles. Overall it is close to the references but slightly lower in craft density, and when in doubt the rule is fail.
